summary.tldr: Creates new privacy and artificial intelligence laws, and sets up a tribunal for some privacy appeals and penalties.
what_it_does: Creates the Consumer Privacy Protection Act to govern how organizations collect, use or disclose personal information in commercial activities.
Repeals Part 1 of the Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act and renames that law the Electronic Documents Act.
Creates the Personal Information and Data Protection Tribunal to hear some Privacy Commissioner appeals and impose penalties for certain breaches.
Creates the Artificial Intelligence and Data Act to regulate certain AI systems in international and interprovincial trade and commerce, and requires risk mitigation measures for high-impact systems.
Requires public reporting and lets the minister order records about artificial intelligence systems.
Bans using illegally obtained personal information to design, develop, use or make available an AI system, and bans making an AI system available if its use causes serious harm.
summary.background: The bill was introduced in the House of Commons on 16 June 2022. It also makes consequential and related amendments to other Acts.
